answers.explanation: The origin is wrong, so origin validation catches it, and RPKI is what's deployed.
RPKI only checks the origin. Only path validation notices a forged path.
BGPsec leverages RPKI's certificates for prefix and AS information.
S-BGP and soBGP were early designs. RPKI is deployed, and BGPsec is the current path-validation standard.
soBGP keeps security out of the update messages to reduce overhead.
Right AS, and /25 is within the allowed length.
The prefix is covered, but by the wrong AS. This is the YouTube-style hijack, caught.
Right AS, but /26 is longer than the ROA's maximum of /25. Max length stops even the owner's AS from being impersonated with a more specific route.
No ROA covers it, so RPKI can't say. Most routers still accept it.
Every AS has to sign every update in real time, and a partial rollout protects very little.
